statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-5713: The asyncio introspection tools (python -m asyncio ps and python -m asyncio pstree) used offset tables read from the target process without validating them, so a privileged process connecting to a malicious Python process through the remote debugging feature could be made to read and write out-of-bounds addresses. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/148178 (3.14 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/316f6265b7f9ca4ffed5346b747475ef1943f35d), first released in CPython 3.14.5; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/OG4RHARYSNIE22GGOMVMCRH76L5HKPLM/; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-5713. Checked the _remote_debugging extension module in every published build, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4, of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package on x86_64 and aarch64 for the offset-table validation the fix adds (its 'Invalid debug offsets' and 'Invalid AsyncioDebug offsets' errors). 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.4-r3 lack the fix; 3.14.4-r4 is the first published build that has it and carries a DHI backport of the upstream fix, ahead of the upstream release, and every later build carries it.

The asyncio introspection tools (python -m asyncio ps and python -m asyncio pstree) and, in 3.15, the profiling.sampling module used offset tables read from the target process without validating them, so a privileged process connecting to a malicious Python process through the remote debugging feature could be made to read and write out-of-bounds addresses. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/148178 (commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/289fd2c97a7e5aecb8b69f94f5e838ccfeee7e67, on the main branch before 3.15 branched; the 3.14 backport is https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/316f6265b7f9ca4ffed5346b747475ef1943f35d), and the CVE record lists 3.15 as affected only from 3.15.0a1 to before 3.15.0b1; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/OG4RHARYSNIE22GGOMVMCRH76L5HKPLM/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-5713. The fix adds Modules/_remote_debugging/debug_offsets_validation.h, which is in the 3.15.0b1, 3.15.0 and 3.15.2 sources and not in 3.15.0a8. Checked the compiled _remote_debugging extension module in the python-3.15 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository by 2026-11-27 (3.15.0-r0 and 3.15.2-r0 to 3.15.2-r4), on x86_64 and aarch64 (each build is CPython 3.15.0 or 3.15.2 by the version string in its libpython3.15.so) for two error messages that only the fix adds, 'Invalid AsyncioDebug offsets' and 'exceeds local buffer size': every build contains both, while the _remote_debugging module of an earlier DHI Python build that predates the fix (python-3.14 3.14.3-r0) contains neither; the module's own 'Invalid debug offsets found' message, present before the fix, is found in all of them. Every published build carries the fix, so the range ends at the lowest published build, 3.15.0-r0.
